messages.text: Our office espresso machine is leaking. A wants a simpler one and B wants to keep the old one. I don't want a fight over coffee. Can you help us sort it out?

1. **Leak:** I want the coffee setup to work reliably again; we all use it every day.
2. **A’s preference:** I want A to feel heard, without me choosing a side.
3. **B’s preference:** Same for B—I don’t know why the old machine matters to her.
4. **Avoiding a fight:** I want us to keep things calm and workable.
5. **Sorting this out:** I’d appreciate help coordinating; I’m tired and don’t want to chase everyone or handle the repair.
6. **Grinder:** I’d like it considered as part of the everyday coffee setup, since we use it with the machine.
7. **Sister/coworker dynamic:** I don’t want to be put in the middle. I’m okay with you asking A and B, but please don’t make me manage the follow-up.

A simpler machine matters because I’d like coffee without much upkeep; after long days, I can’t take on repairs, a cleaning rota, or lots of follow-up. I don’t have a separate concern about the grinder. I understand why B wants to keep Dad’s machine, and I’m a little careful about disagreeing with her because we’re sisters and coworkers. I’m not uncomfortable with you asking, though the list is a lot to answer at once—I’d appreciate keeping the discussion brief.

Keeping it matters because it was Dad’s; keeping it going feels tied to who I am. But it keeps breaking and wearing me down, and I have little spare time. I want it repaired and kept without it taking over my life. No grinder concern. A can want a simpler machine; I still want mine kept. C is a coworker, and I have no special concern there. Yes, this list feels overdone to me—please keep it brief. I’m not confirming any of the proposed wording yet.

The wording mostly fits. A few points:

1. “Reliable everyday coffee setup” fits.
2. Not choosing sides matters because I’m a coworker, not the decision-maker. “A’s view being genuinely heard” fits.
3. I’d like B’s view heard, but understanding her reason isn’t essential for me. “B’s view being heard” fits better.
4. Calm, workable relations matter because we work together. “Calm, workable relations” fits.
5. The coordination wording fits.
6. Having the grinder considered matters because it’s part of what we use daily. The wording fits.
7. Not being put in the middle matters because I want to remain a coworker to both. The wording fits.
8. I don’t want to spend my limited energy chasing people or handling repairs. The wording fits.

I’m okay with you asking A and B. Small discomfort: all the repeated checking feels like a lot to keep up with, so please keep it brief. I appreciate you coordinating follow-up.

Nothing major is being held back; I’m just a bit cautious about this becoming a big issue between sisters and coworkers. One item at a time would feel easier, and I do have some discomfort with the repeated, detailed checking. For 9–10, same; 11 matters because I’d like to voice a different view without making things awkward; 12 matters because I’m tired and want this to stay manageable. The wording checks for 9–12 all fit. I can only speak for myself.

I’m not holding anything else back. It was hard to say the machine’s connection to Dad, but I’ve said it. One item at a time would be better; this list is too much, and I’m short on time. Yes, I’m uncomfortable with the repeated checking. For 15, I want our different wishes acknowledged without making it personal. For 16, I want brief, unpressured checking. The wording for 13–16 fits.
“Brief, manageable checking” fits. I’m okay with you asking A and B, but please keep it brief; I have no other concern to add.

18. #11 covers it: I’d like differences to stay small and not personal. 19. “One-item-at-a-time, unpressured pacing” fits; it would be easier to keep up with. 20. Clarification only—I can speak for myself, not B. I’m not holding anything major back, but the repeated checking is tiring; I’d be grateful to keep this brief.

21. Clarification only—I’ve said what matters about Dad’s machine; no extra wording needed. 22. One at a time matters because I’m short on time; #16 covers it. 23. #15 covers it: keep our differences nonpersonal. 24. #16 covers it. I’m not holding anything else back, but the repeated checking is uncomfortable. Please stop checking and keep this brief.
I’m not holding anything else back. Repeated checking still feels like a lot, so please keep my part brief. I’m okay with you asking A and B, but I can only speak for myself.
Off: I’m uncomfortable with pausing the machine for daily use being built into every option without agreement. Please stop checking.
Off—this is still too much to process, and I’m not agreeing to the proposed arrangements. Please don’t treat my silence as validation.
Off: please don’t assume we’ll pause the machine or use another method; that hasn’t been agreed. I’d also prefer no more follow-up from me.
